chapter.title: Plugging in your work apps

cards.body: Your workflow can read the clock, but it cannot open a single spreadsheet. It has no badge. On the assembly line, a station that fetches parts from the warehouse wears a key card on a lanyard. In n8n that key card is a *credential*: **a saved permission for n8n to act as you** inside one app, such as Google Sheets or Slack. The station is the node. The badge is a separate thing, and the badge is what opens the door.
cards.simpler: Your workflow can tell the time, but it cannot open your spreadsheet. It has no permission yet. Think of a worker who fetches parts from a locked storeroom. They need a key card on a lanyard. In n8n that key card is a credential: **a saved permission for n8n to act as you** inside one app, like Google Sheets or Slack. The worker is the node. The key card is separate, and the key card opens the door.

cards.prompt: Priya drops a Google Sheets node onto her canvas, picks 'Append row', hits Test step, and n8n stops with a warning before it touches any sheet. What is she missing?

options.text: A second Google Sheets node, because one is never enough
A credential, so n8n is allowed to act as her Google account
A Schedule Trigger, because nothing runs without a bell

whyNot.a: That's the station, not the badge: a second node still has no permission to open her sheet.
whyNot.c: That's the bell from chapter 1, not the badge: Test step runs the node by hand, so the trigger isn't what stopped her.

cards.reteach: The node knows how to append a row. It does not have the right to. Google asks: who is this, and did they say yes? The credential is the saved yes, made once and picked from a dropdown in the node.

cards.title: What the badge is
cards.body:
A Slack or Gmail node knows how to do the job. It does not have the right to do it. The app on the far end asks: who is this, and did they agree? The credential answers for you.

On n8n Cloud, for the big apps, making one is a sign-in button. Click *Create new credential*, a Google or Slack window opens, it lists what n8n wants to do, you click Allow. n8n keeps a *token*, a long code that stands in for your password, so your password is never typed into n8n.

You'd think the node holds the login. It doesn't. **The credential lives on its own** in the Credentials page, and the node only points at it.
cards.simpler: A Slack or Gmail node knows how to do the job, but it has no permission. The credential is that permission. For big apps, you sign in: a Google or Slack window lists what n8n wants to do, and you click Allow. n8n keeps a token, a long code that stands in for your password, so your password never goes into n8n. **The credential lives on its own** in the Credentials page, and the node only points at it.

cards.title: Dana and the callbacks sheet
cards.body: Dana runs the front desk at a dental clinic and keeps missed-call callbacks in a Google Sheet. In n8n she adds a Google Sheets node, chooses 'Append row', and clicks Create new credential. A Google window opens, says n8n wants to see and edit her spreadsheets, and she clicks Allow. The window closes and n8n shows a green tick that the connection tested fine. Back in the node, the sheet field now offers a list, and 'Patient callbacks' is sitting right there, because **n8n is now looking at Drive with her eyes**.
cards.simpler: Dana works the front desk at a dental clinic. She tracks missed-call callbacks in a Google Sheet. In n8n she adds a Google Sheets node, picks Append row, and clicks Create new credential. A Google window says n8n wants to see and edit her spreadsheets. She clicks Allow. n8n shows a green tick, meaning the connection works. Back in the node, the sheet dropdown now lists Patient callbacks, because **n8n is now looking at Drive with her eyes**.

cards.prompt: Marcus connected Slack last week for a workflow that posts daily sales. Today he builds a second workflow that also posts to Slack. What does he do in the new Slack node?

options.text: Click Create new credential and sign in to Slack again from scratch
Open the credential dropdown and pick the Slack credential he already has
Paste his Slack password into the node's message field

whyNot.a: That's making a second badge for the same door: it works, but the point of a credential is to make it once and reuse it.
whyNot.c: That's mixing the badge into the message: the message field is what gets posted, and n8n never wants your password typed into a node.

cards.reteach: The badge is not part of any one node. It sits on its own in the Credentials page, and every Slack node in every workflow can point at the same one. Make it once, pick it many times.

cards.title: One badge, many stations
cards.body:
Because the badge is separate, you make it once. Every Slack node in every workflow can pick the same credential from the dropdown. When someone leaves the team, you delete that one credential and every node that used it stops. That is exactly what you want.

Keep two things straight. **The credential says who; the node's settings say what.** 'Append a row to Patient callbacks' is the node. 'As dana@clinic' is the badge.

Name badges by account. *Google Sheets, work, dana@* beats *Google Sheets account 2*, especially in three weeks when you have four of them and one belongs to a laptop you no longer own.
cards.simpler: Because the badge is separate, you make it once. Any Slack node in any workflow can pick the same credential. When someone leaves the team, you delete that one credential and every node using it stops. Keep two things apart. **The credential says who; the node's settings say what.** Append a row to Patient callbacks is the node. As dana@clinic is the badge. Name badges by account. Google Sheets, work, dana@ beats Google Sheets account 2 once you have four of them.

cards.body: Rahul connects Google Sheets, opens the sheet dropdown in his node, and sees only 'Fantasy league 2024' and 'Flat deposit'. He spends 10 minutes convinced the work sheet is broken. It isn't; he clicked Allow while signed in to his personal Gmail. Spot it: **when the list of sheets, channels or labels looks like someone else's life, you have the wrong badge**, not a bad node. Make a second credential with the work account and name it so.
cards.simpler: Rahul connects Google Sheets, opens the sheet dropdown, and sees only Fantasy league 2024 and Flat deposit. He spends ten minutes sure the work sheet is broken. It isn't. He clicked Allow while signed in to his personal Gmail. The sign to look for: **when the list of sheets, channels or labels looks like someone else's life, you have the wrong badge**, not a bad node. Make a second credential with the work account and name it clearly.

cards.prompt: Which line is true about a credential in n8n?

options.text: It tells n8n what to do, such as append a row or send a message
It tells n8n which account to act as, and the node's settings say what to do
Each node needs its own fresh one, even for the same app and account

whyNot.a: That's the node's job, not the badge's: the operation is chosen inside the node, the credential only says who.
whyNot.c: That's the opposite of why badges live separately: one credential is made once and shared by every node that needs that account.

cards.reteach: Picture the badge on the lanyard and the station on the belt. The station decides the job. The badge decides whose name is on the job. One badge opens the door for as many stations as you like.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
A credential is a badge: your saved yes that lets n8n act as you in one app, made once and reused by any node. The node decides what to do; **the badge decides who it does it as**.

Tomorrow: how a customer's name travels from station 1 to station 3.
cards.simpler: A credential is a badge. It is your saved yes that lets n8n act as you inside one app. You make it once, and any node can reuse it. The node decides what to do; **the badge decides who it does it as**. Tomorrow we look at how a customer's name travels from station 1 to station 3.

cards.body: Open n8n, click Credentials in the left menu, and create one for an app you use at work. Name it with the account's email. Then add a node for that app and watch the dropdown fill up.
cards.simpler: Open n8n and click Credentials in the left menu. Create one for an app you use at work. **Name it with the account's email address** so you always know whose it is. Then add a node for that app and pick that credential. Watch the dropdown fill up with your real sheets, channels or labels.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now connect one work app to n8n and make it add a row or send a message as you.
